name: acm_fat_attr_from_mode
prototype: int acm_fat_attr_from_mode(const SceSelfAuthInfo *info, const acm_ctx *ctx, u32 mode)
notes: types 1..5 of kscePfsACSetFSAttrByMode. mode 0x1000000 -> attribute = 0x0F (u16 0x000F for 2-byte attributes), the special system value. Otherwise, by thread access level: 0x40/0x80 look up mode & 0x10186 in 0x810027c4: 0x10186/0x186 -> 0, 0x10106 -> 1, 0x106 -> 4, 0x10104/0x104 -> 5, 0x10006/0x6 -> 6, 0x10004/0x4 -> 7. 0x10/0x20 look up mode & 0x180: 0x180 -> 0, 0x100 -> 1. Other levels or an unlisted mode -> 0x80010016. The result goes through acm_attr_set3. In FAT terms 1 = READONLY, 2 = HIDDEN, 4 = SYSTEM: user rw -> plain, user r -> read-only, system-only -> SYSTEM|HIDDEN(|RO). Mode bits are SCE_S_IRUSR 0x100, IWUSR 0x80, IRSYS 4, IWSYS 2; the 0x10000 flag only separates 1 from 4 for 0x106

name: acm_fat_check_access
prototype: int acm_fat_check_access(const SceSelfAuthInfo *info, const acm_ctx *ctx, u32 req)
notes: types 1..5 of acm_check_access. Allowed access by attribute & 7, from the calling thread access level: 0x10/0x20 table 0x81002834 {0xB, 9, 0xB, 9, 1, 1, 0, 0}; 0x40/0x80 table 0x81002864 {0xB, 0xB, 0xB, 0xB, 0xB, 9, 0xB, 9}; other levels -> 0x8001000D. Access bits: 1 read, 2 write, 8 (the third right). (allowed & req) == req -> 0, else 0x8001000D. Types 1..3 need a 1-byte, 4..5 a 2-byte attribute (else 0x800F0916). Net effect: READONLY blocks writes for user threads only, SYSTEM leaves user threads read-only, SYSTEM|HIDDEN hides the entry from them, and privileged threads lose write only on SYSTEM|READONLY

name: acm_pfs_attr_from_mode
prototype: int acm_pfs_attr_from_mode(const SceSelfAuthInfo *info, const acm_ctx *ctx, u32 mode)
notes: type 6. The program class is capability word 0 (info+0x10): 0x10 or 0x20 user, 0x40 or 0x80 privileged, else 0x800F0928. Mode bits 0x00F00000 are rejected for user classes (0x80010016) and 0x00C00000 for privileged ones. Mode & 0x10186 (privileged, table 0x810028dc: 0x186 -> 0, 0x10106 -> 1, 0x106 -> 4, 0x104 -> 5, 0x6 -> 6, 0x4 -> 7) or & 0x180 (user, 0x810028cc: 0x180 -> 0, 0x100 -> 1) gives the low bits; unlisted -> 0x800F0902. mode 0x100000 adds 0x4000 and 0x200000 adds 0x2000. Stored whole with acm_pfs_attr_store
